kind: Native MCP catalog handshake only; no model calls or browser tasks

opencode.instructions:
browse drives the user's real Chrome-family browser through the browse extension, so logins, extensions and open tabs are already there and the user can watch or take over.

Tabs are the handle. `navigate` with a `url` and no `tab` opens a new background tab and returns its id as `tab`; keep it and pass `tab` to every other call (snapshot, click, fill, screenshot, ...). `navigate` with `tab` goes to a URL in that tab. Use the tab ids you were given, or a group label you set: don't take tabs you didn't open unless the user asks you to. Popups a page opens show up as `newTabs` in a result and are yours to use. `tabs` lists every agent tab and the ones the user lent (they click the browse toolbar button on a tab; use it by its id).

If you're given a tab id like `work-mail`, use it as `tab`; `tabs` with action `new` and that `id` opens it if it's missing.

Use one loop: inspect, act, verify.
- Inspect with `snapshot` before choosing anything. It returns an accessibility tree with refs like `e12`; pass a ref (with the same `tab`) to `click`, `fill`, `type`, `select`, `hover` or `drag`. Refs go stale after the page changes: snapshot again.
- Act with the narrowest stable control. Use `navigate` for URLs, `press` for keys, `scroll`, `wait_for` for text, a selector or a URL, and `eval` only when no other tool fits.
- Verify with a fresh read (`snapshot`, `screenshot`, or `eval` of the URL). A click that returned is not proof the task succeeded.

In code mode, compose these tools in one script: navigate, call `snapshot`, pick refs from its text, act, then snapshot again to check, all in one run instead of one tool call per turn.

When only a person can proceed — login, 2FA, passkey, captcha or payment confirmation — call `handoff` with the `tab` and what the user should do, and wait. Never solve a captcha yourself and never retry-loop a blocked site.

When finished, close the tabs you opened (`tabs` with action `close`; `group` closes every tab you opened with that group label). `status` reports the relay and the connected browsers.

If a call fails because no browser is connected (the extension isn't added, paired or open), `status` says why in `nextStep`: pass that step to the user and wait for them instead of retrying.

tools.name: status
tools.description: Report the relay, the connected browsers (ids to pass as `browser` when opening a tab), pairing state and what to do when no browser is connected (`nextStep`), and the tabs you can use.

tools.name: tabs
tools.description: List, open or close tabs. Tabs are the handle every other tool takes as `tab`. `list` returns every agent tab and every tab the user lent (tab id, id when one was chosen, url, title, group, options, lent, lastUsed, busy and browser). An id or group from that list tells you which tabs you opened; use only those unless the user asks you to touch another. `new` opens a background tab (at `url`, else about:blank), waits for it to load and returns its `tab` id; `navigate` without `tab` does the same. Give it an `id` like `work-mail` to name the tab yourself: opening that id again returns the tab it already names, without navigating it, and the id survives browser restarts (use it as `tab` in every tool). `close` needs explicit tabs: `tab`, `tabs` or a whole `group`; a lent tab is given back to the user instead of closed. Tabs open in the background and never take focus from the user; close the ones you opened when you're done.

group.description: new: the new tab's group label. list: only that group's tabs. close: close every tab opened with that group (and their popups).

allowedOrigins.description: When opening a tab: hosts or origins it may load (example.com, *.example.com, https://app.example.com, http://localhost:3000). Navigations elsewhere are refused or sent back to about:blank; private and loopback addresses need an exact entry. Popups inherit it.

readOnly.description: When opening a tab: only read it (snapshots, screenshots, page state); input and later navigation are refused.

keepVisible.description: When opening a tab: keep it focused to the page between calls, for apps that pause while hidden. Pages can notice.

browser.description: When opening a tab: which connected browser, by the id or name `status` lists. Defaults to the first connected one.

action.description: What to do. Defaults to list.

id.description: new: an id you choose for the tab, like `work-mail` (lowercase letters, digits and dashes). Every tool takes it as `tab`. Opening with an id that already exists returns that tab without navigating it; the tab keeps the id when the browser restarts, and is never closed as idle.

url.description: new: the URL to open (else about:blank).

tab.description: close: the tab to close: its numeric id, or a chosen id like `work-mail`.

tabs.description: close: several tabs to close, by numeric or chosen id.

idleMinutes.description: close: only tabs no call used for this long. It narrows tab, tabs or group; it doesn't pick tabs on its own, and never a tab with a chosen id.

tools.name: handoff
tools.description: Ask the user to do something in a tab only a person can do (sign in, 2FA, a captcha, a payment confirmation) and wait until they finish. The tab shows a card with your message and a Continue button (the browse toolbar button also continues). Returns `outcome`: continued, timeout, closed (the tab went away) or cancelled. Never solve a captcha yourself; hand it off. Re-read the page afterwards: it has probably changed.

message.description: What the user should do, in one or two plain sentences, e.g. "Sign in to GitHub, then click Continue."

tab.description: The tab to act on: the id navigate or tabs new returned (or a lent tab's id from tabs list), or a chosen id like `work-mail` given to tabs new.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long to wait for the user. Defaults to 600.

tools.name: demonstrate
tools.description: Ask the user to show you a flow in a tab, recording what they do until they click Continue: clicks (with a CSS selector, role and name), fills (password values are never recorded), checkbox and select changes, and navigations. Use it when you can't find how to do something and the user can show you. Returns `steps` (structured) and `summary` (one line each) to repeat with the page tools.

message.description: What the user should demonstrate, e.g. "Show me how to export the report, then click Continue."

tab.description: The tab to act on: the id navigate or tabs new returned (or a lent tab's id from tabs list), or a chosen id like `work-mail` given to tabs new.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long to wait for the user. Defaults to 600.

tools.name: settings
tools.description: Read or change the user's browse settings from the extension's options page: where agent tabs open (window), how they're grouped (grouping), when untouched agent tabs close (idleMinutes), human-like input (humanInput) and handoff notifications (handoffNotifications). Use it only when the user asks to change how browse behaves. Without `set` it returns each setting's stored value, the value in effect and the relay environment variable that overrides it, if any. With `set` it validates every value, applies the change at once and returns what changed: tell the user what you changed. Security switches (OPENCODE_BROWSER_ALLOW_ALL_COOKIES, OPENCODE_BROWSER_ALLOW_FOREGROUND, OPENCODE_BROWSER_ALLOW_ALL_STORAGE, OPENCODE_BROWSER_ALLOW_FILE_URLS, OPENCODE_BROWSER_UPDATE_CHECK) are environment-only and can't be read or changed here.

set.description: Settings to change; omit to only read them.

window.description: Where agents open their tabs (current: the user's window; separate: an unfocused window of their own)

grouping.description: How agent tabs are grouped (one shared group, one group per agent group label, or none)

idleMinutes.description: Close agent tabs untouched for this many minutes

humanInput.description: Human-like input (off is faster, but easier for sites to flag)

handoffNotifications.description: System notification on a handoff (only while recorded, or every handoff)

tools.name: navigate
tools.description: Open a page. Without `tab` it opens a new background tab at `url` and returns its id as `tab`: keep it and pass it to every other tool (the options group, allowedOrigins, readOnly, keepVisible and browser apply to the new tab and the popups it opens). With `tab` it goes to `url` in that tab, or back/forward/reload, and waits for the page. Returns JSON: tab, url, title, status (the HTTP status, when known), navigated, from, and when relevant redirects, pending (a navigation still loading when the timeout hit; url is what the tab shows meanwhile), dialog, newTabs, challenge (a bot check or block page was detected; follow its warning, usually handoff) and warning. An HTTP error status is a result, not a failure. A bare host gets https:// (":3000" means http://localhost:3000); http(s), about:blank, data:, blob:, file: and view-source: URLs are used as given; javascript: (use eval) and app schemes such as mailto: or tel: are refused. Navigations outside the tab's domain allowlist are refused.

group.description: When opening a tab: a label for it (and the popups it opens), e.g. the task's name. It is the tab group's title in the browser, and `tabs` can list or close a whole group at once.

allowedOrigins.description: When opening a tab: hosts or origins it may load (example.com, *.example.com, https://app.example.com, http://localhost:3000). Navigations elsewhere are refused or sent back to about:blank; private and loopback addresses need an exact entry. Popups inherit it.

readOnly.description: When opening a tab: only read it (snapshots, screenshots, page state); input and later navigation are refused.

keepVisible.description: When opening a tab: keep it focused to the page between calls, for apps that pause while hidden. Pages can notice.

browser.description: When opening a tab: which connected browser, by the id or name `status` lists. Defaults to the first connected one.

url.description: Where to go. Required for goto.

action.description: Default goto when url is given.

waitUntil.description: load (default); settle also waits for the network and DOM to go quiet (good before a snapshot of an app); commit returns once the new document starts.

timeout.description: Milliseconds the whole navigation may take, including a slow server (default 30000). Timing out is a warning, not an error.

tab.description: The tab to navigate: its id (from an earlier navigate or tabs) or a chosen id like `work-mail`. Leave it out to open a new tab.

tools.name: snapshot
tools.description: A compact outline of the page for deciding what to do next: headings, landmarks, lists, tables, dialogs and every interactive element with a ref, e.g. `- button "Save" [ref=e12]`. Refs stay the same across snapshots while the element does, and are valid until the page navigates; pass them to click/fill/etc. Iframe content is nested under its iframe line and its refs work too. Auto-scopes to the open modal dialog, or to <main> (plus header controls) when there is one; a note then says how many landmarks and controls outside <main> are not shown, and within "body" includes them. Use find to grep (with context lines), diff/delta to see only what changed since the last snapshot, interactive to list only controls, within to scope to a ref or selector. mode "aria" returns Playwright's full ARIA tree instead (refs like a5).

within.description: A ref ("e12") or selector to snapshot only that part. A selector with several matches uses the first visible one, with no match the whole page; either adds a note.

interactive.description: Only controls (and alerts), no headings or paragraphs.

compact.description: Collapse link-only navigation, layout tables and redundant headings (default true).

find.description: Only lines containing this text (case-insensitive), or matching /regex/flags, with context lines around them; also searches inside collapsed navigation.

context.description: Context lines around find matches (0-10, default 2).

diff.description: Only +added / -removed lines versus the previous snapshot (same tab and options required).

delta.description: Like diff when a compatible previous snapshot exists, else a full snapshot.

maxItems.description: Most lines (1-200, default 80); important items are kept first.

mode.description: compact (default) or aria (Playwright's ARIA snapshot in AI mode, with editable values redacted).

tab.description: The tab to act on: the id navigate or tabs new returned (or a lent tab's id from tabs list), or a chosen id like `work-mail` given to tabs new.

tools.name: click
tools.description: Click an element (or x/y in page CSS pixels). Waits until it is visible, enabled and not moving, scrolls it into view and checks nothing covers it: a covered target fails fast naming the element on top (dismiss it, or pass force). Returns JSON: clicked, url, and what changed: navigated/title, urlChanged, dialog (the page is paused until you call dialog), newTabs, challenge/warning.

position.description: Click point relative to the element's top-left corner instead of its center.

timeout.description: Milliseconds to wait for the element (default 10000).

ref.description: Address elements by `ref` from the latest snapshot ("e12"; "a5" / "f1a5" from an aria snapshot) or by `selector`: CSS, or Playwright selectors such as `role=button[name="Save"]`, `text=Sign in`, `label=Email`, `placeholder=Search`, `testid=submit`, chained with `>>` (`form >> role=button`, `>> nth=0`). Enter an iframe with `iframe[title="Pay"] >> frame >> role=button[name="Pay"]`.

selector.description: CSS or Playwright selector, used when there is no ref. Must match exactly one element.

tab.description: The tab to act on: the id navigate or tabs new returned (or a lent tab's id from tabs list), or a chosen id like `work-mail` given to tabs new.

tools.name: fill
tools.description: Fill form fields with trusted input, replacing what is there: text inputs, textareas and contenteditable get the value typed in; selects pick the option by value or label; checkboxes/radios/switches take checked. Fill one field with ref/selector + value|checked, or many with fields: [...]. submit presses Enter after the last field. Returns JSON: filled (per field) and what changed.

checked.description: For a checkbox, radio or switch.

fields.description: Several fields in order, instead of ref/selector + value.

ref.description: Address elements by `ref` from the latest snapshot ("e12"; "a5" / "f1a5" from an aria snapshot) or by `selector`: CSS, or Playwright selectors such as `role=button[name="Save"]`, `text=Sign in`, `label=Email`, `placeholder=Search`, `testid=submit`, chained with `>>` (`form >> role=button`, `>> nth=0`). Enter an iframe with `iframe[title="Pay"] >> frame >> role=button[name="Pay"]`.

selector.description: CSS or Playwright selector, used when there is no ref. Must match exactly one element.

tab.description: The tab to act on: the id navigate or tabs new returned (or a lent tab's id from tabs list), or a chosen id like `work-mail` given to tabs new.

tools.name: type
tools.description: Type text key by key into the focused element, or into ref/selector after focusing it (with human input on, it clicks into it first). Unlike fill it does not clear the field, and fires real key events; use it for search boxes with suggestions, editors and key handlers. submit presses Enter afterwards.

selector.description: CSS or Playwright selector, used when there is no ref. Must match exactly one element.

tab.description: The tab to act on: the id navigate or tabs new returned (or a lent tab's id from tabs list), or a chosen id like `work-mail` given to tabs new.

tools.name: press
tools.description: Press a key or shortcut on the focused element (or ref/selector after focusing it): "Enter", "Escape", "Tab", "ArrowDown", "PageDown", "Control+A", "ControlOrMeta+K", "Shift+Tab". key can be a list pressed in order; count repeats it.

count.description: Repeat the key(s), e.g. 3 x ArrowDown.

selector.description: CSS or Playwright selector, used when there is no ref. Must match exactly one element.

tab.description: The tab to act on: the id navigate or tabs new returned (or a lent tab's id from tabs list), or a chosen id like `work-mail` given to tabs new.

tools.name: select
tools.description: Select option(s) of a <select> by value or label (by: "value", "label" or "index" to be strict). Several values for a multiple select. Returns the selected values. For custom dropdowns (role=combobox/listbox), click the control and then the option instead.

selector.description: CSS or Playwright selector, used when there is no ref. Must match exactly one element.

tab.description: The tab to act on: the id navigate or tabs new returned (or a lent tab's id from tabs list), or a chosen id like `work-mail` given to tabs new.

tools.name: hover
tools.description: Move the pointer over an element (or x/y) to open menus or tooltips; then snapshot to see what appeared.

selector.description: CSS or Playwright selector, used when there is no ref. Must match exactly one element.

tab.description: The tab to act on: the id navigate or tabs new returned (or a lent tab's id from tabs list), or a chosen id like `work-mail` given to tabs new.

tools.name: drag
tools.description: Drag from one element or point to another with the mouse (HTML5 drag and drop included). from/to are a ref or selector string, or { ref | selector | x, y }.

tab.description: The tab to act on: the id navigate or tabs new returned (or a lent tab's id from tabs list), or a chosen id like `work-mail` given to tabs new.

tools.name: scroll
tools.description: Scroll with the mouse wheel by deltaX/deltaY pixels (over ref/selector, or the page), jump to an edge with to ("top", "bottom"; of the element when given), or scroll ref/selector into view. Returns scrollY, scrollHeight, viewportHeight and atBottom, so loops can stop at the end of an infinite list.

selector.description: CSS or Playwright selector, used when there is no ref. Must match exactly one element.

tab.description: The tab to act on: the id navigate or tabs new returned (or a lent tab's id from tabs list), or a chosen id like `work-mail` given to tabs new.

tools.name: eval
tools.description: Run JavaScript in the page and return its result as JSON. An expression's value is returned (promises are awaited, await works). Statements (const/let, loops, several lines) return the value of their last expression statement, like a console (`const a = 3; a` gives 3), or what they `return`. Declarations stay local to the call and never leak into the page. DOM nodes come back as "<tag#id.class>", Map as an object, Set as an array, Date as an ISO string, Errors as {name, message}, cycles as "[Circular]". A script still running at the timeout is stopped. By default it runs in browse's isolated world: it sees the DOM but not the page's own JS globals, and the page can't see it. world "main" runs in the page's own world (window variables, frameworks) and is visible to it. With ref/selector or arg, expression must be a function, called as (element, arg) => ...; e.g. expression "(el) => el.href" with ref "e5". Without them, a function written as the whole expression is called with no arguments, so "() => document.title" works like "document.title". frame (a selector of an <iframe>) runs in that frame. Results over 100k characters are cut.

expression.description: An expression, statements whose last value is returned, or a function: (element, arg) => ... when ref/selector/arg is given, else called with no arguments.

arg.description: A JSON value passed as the function's second argument.

frame.description: Selector of an <iframe> to run in, when there is no ref.

selector.description: CSS or Playwright selector, used when there is no ref. Must match exactly one element.

tab.description: The tab to act on: the id navigate or tabs new returned (or a lent tab's id from tabs list), or a chosen id like `work-mail` given to tabs new.

tools.name: wait_for
tools.description: Wait until conditions hold (all of them): text appears (or textGone disappears) in the page (case-insensitive and whitespace-normalized like Playwright's text=, unless exact), the url matches (url: a substring, a glob with * and **, or /regex/flags when the body uses regex syntax; urlRegex: a regular expression), ref/selector reaches state (visible by default, hidden, attached, detached), or the page reaches load (load, domcontentloaded, settle, or commit; a navigation in flight is waited for first). ms just sleeps first. Fails with what it was waiting for on timeout.

text.description: Text that must appear; case-insensitive substring unless exact.

url.description: Substring ("/checkout" matches any URL containing it), glob ("**/orders/*"), or /regex/flags; it is a regex only when the part between the slashes uses regex syntax (\ ^ $ * + ? ( ) [ ] { } |), so a path like /docs/us stays a substring.

urlRegex.description: A regular expression the URL must match, without slashes, e.g. "/orders/\d+$". Prefix (?i) for case-insensitive.

load.description: commit waits for a navigation in flight to commit.

selector.description: CSS or Playwright selector, used when there is no ref. Must match exactly one element.

tab.description: The tab to act on: the id navigate or tabs new returned (or a lent tab's id from tabs list), or a chosen id like `work-mail` given to tabs new.

tools.name: dialog
tools.description: Answer a JavaScript alert/confirm/prompt: action accept (with promptText for a prompt) or dismiss. While one is open the page is paused and other tools fail with its message. status shows the open dialog. auto: "accept" or "dismiss" answers future dialogs on the tab automatically ("off" to stop); beforeunload dialogs are always accepted.

promptText.description: The answer to a prompt() dialog, for action accept or with auto "accept".

tab.description: The tab to act on: the id navigate or tabs new returned (or a lent tab's id from tabs list), or a chosen id like `work-mail` given to tabs new.

tools.name: upload
tools.description: Set the files of a file input (input[type=file], or its label) without opening the file chooser. files are absolute paths inside browse's file roots, on the machine browse runs on; browse reads them and hands the page in-memory copies (with input and change events), so the browser may be elsewhere. At most 50 MB per call.

selector.description: CSS or Playwright selector, used when there is no ref. Must match exactly one element.

tab.description: The tab to act on: the id navigate or tabs new returned (or a lent tab's id from tabs list), or a chosen id like `work-mail` given to tabs new.

tools.name: emulate
tools.description: Change how the tab presents itself: viewport { width, height, deviceScaleFactor, mobile } (or "reset"), colorScheme, reducedMotion, forcedColors, contrast, media ("print"), userAgent, geolocation { latitude, longitude } (the site still needs the user's permission), touch, offline. "reset" restores a setting. Permissions can't be granted.

tab.description: The tab to act on: the id navigate or tabs new returned (or a lent tab's id from tabs list), or a chosen id like `work-mail` given to tabs new.

tools.name: webmcp
tools.description: Use tools the page itself offers through WebMCP (navigator.modelContext), in any frame. action list returns { available, tools: [{ name, description, inputSchema, frame }] }; action call runs one by name with input and returns its result. Prefer a site's WebMCP tool over clicking when it does what you need. Tools are read in browse's isolated world; when a page defines modelContext only in its own world (a polyfill), browse reads and calls them there, which the page can observe (such tools show world "main").

frame.description: When a tool name exists in several frames: the frame label or URL from list.

tab.description: The tab to act on: the id navigate or tabs new returned (or a lent tab's id from tabs list), or a chosen id like `work-mail` given to tabs new.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: Capture the tab as an image: the viewport (default), the full page, one element (a snapshot ref, including refs inside iframes, or a selector, resolved exactly like the page tools) or a rectangle (clip, viewport CSS pixels). By default image pixels are CSS pixels, so a point (x, y) in a viewport screenshot is the same (x, y) mouse tools use. Returns the image, or saves it to path and returns {path, width, height} (actual image pixels). Inline images are scaled down to at most 8000 px per side, saved ones to 16384 px (a note says so). fullPage on a page taller or wider than the viewport, and clips reaching outside it, make Chrome briefly resize the page (pages see resize events); elements are scrolled into view instead when they fit. labels: true numbers the visible interactive elements on the image (drawn on the PNG, nothing is added to the page) and returns [{label, role, text, context, selector, rect:[x,y,w,h]}] so an element seen in the image can be targeted by selector or by its rect's center.

tab.description: The tab to act on: the id navigate or tabs new returned (or a lent tab's id from tabs list), or a chosen id like `work-mail` given to tabs new.

format.description: Image format (default png; jpeg/webp are much smaller).

fullPage.description: Capture the whole scrollable page instead of the viewport.

ref.description: Snapshot ref of the element to capture (e.g. "e12" or an iframe ref "f1e3"); from the tab's latest snapshot.

selector.description: Selector of the element to capture, as the page tools accept it.

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait for the ref/selector element (default 5000).

clip.description: Rectangle to capture, in viewport CSS pixels (as from getBoundingClientRect).

scale.description: css (default): one image pixel per CSS pixel. device: full device resolution (e.g. 2x on Retina).

labels.description: Number visible interactive elements on a viewport PNG and list them.

path.description: Save here instead of returning the image: absolute inside the file roots (in a private folder you own, not directly in a shared temp folder), or relative (saved in a private folder in the first root). Replaces an existing file.

tools.name: screenshot_diff
tools.description: Compare a fresh PNG screenshot of the tab with a baseline PNG saved earlier by screenshot (same region options and scale, since images are never resized). Returns {matches, changedPixels, totalPixels, changedRatio, width, height}; when anything changed, also the diff image (changes red, the rest faded gray) unless diffPath saves it. Use to check whether an action changed the page.

baseline.description: PNG to compare against, inside the file roots.

tab.description: The tab to act on: the id navigate or tabs new returned (or a lent tab's id from tabs list), or a chosen id like `work-mail` given to tabs new.

ref.description: Snapshot ref of the element to compare.

selector.description: Selector of the element to compare.

scale.description: Must match how the baseline was taken (default css).

threshold.description: Per-pixel color tolerance (default 0.1); not an allowance for changed area.

diffPath.description: Save the diff PNG here instead of returning it.

currentPath.description: Also save the fresh screenshot here (e.g. as the next baseline).

tools.name: network
tools.description: Capture a tab's network traffic. One capture per tab. start begins capturing (filters optional); status returns counters only; stop ends it and returns every exchange (method, url, headers, status, bodies; 1000 requests max); cancel discards it. JSON, form and multipart bodies are returned as text (≤1 MB each, 25 MB per capture); other bodies (HTML, scripts, CSS, images, ...) are never fetched and only described {mimeType, size, omitted}, since they can't be checked for credentials. If the tab closes the capture ends and the next stop still returns what it captured, with endedBecause. Credentials are always replaced with [redacted]: authorization and API-key headers, all cookie values, secret-named query/fragment/JSON/form fields, token-like path segments, and any captured secret value wherever it reappears. A capture ends itself after maxDurationMs.

tab.description: The tab to act on: the id navigate or tabs new returned (or a lent tab's id from tabs list), or a chosen id like `work-mail` given to tabs new.

urlFilter.description: start: capture only URLs containing this text.

resourceTypes.description: start: capture only these CDP resource types, e.g. ["XHR", "Fetch", "Document"].

methods.description: start: capture only these HTTP methods, e.g. ["POST"].

bodies.description: start: capture request and response bodies (default true).

maxDurationMs.description: start: end and discard the capture after this long (default 1800000).

tools.name: console
tools.description: Opt-in capture of a tab's own console messages and uncaught errors. Off by default because it enables the CDP Runtime domain, which pages (and bot checks) can detect; stop it when done. Includes out-of-process iframes and workers, and browser log entries such as CSP violations and failed resource loads (with a source); browse's own scripts are left out. start begins capturing (earlier messages are not included); read returns buffered entries {seq, type, text, source, target, url, line} oldest first and by default removes the ones it returned; stop ends the capture. The buffer keeps the newest 1000 entries. If the tab closes the capture ends and read says so.

tab.description: The tab to act on: the id navigate or tabs new returned (or a lent tab's id from tabs list), or a chosen id like `work-mail` given to tabs new.

errorsOnly.description: read: only console.error/assert and uncaught errors.

filter.description: read: only entries whose text contains this (case-insensitive).

since.description: read: only entries with seq greater than this (use a previous lastSeq).

clear.description: read: remove the returned entries from the buffer (default true).

tools.name: recording
tools.description: Record a tab to a video file through the CDP screencast (nothing is shown in or added to the page; the tab doesn't need focus). One recording per tab. start begins recording to path: .mkv writes MJPEG Matroska directly at device resolution (no ffmpeg needed; plays in VLC/mpv/ffmpeg, not browsers), .webm (VP8) or .mp4 (H.264) are transcoded with ffmpeg at CSS viewport size when it stops. status reports duration and frame counters; stop finishes the file and returns {path, bytes, durationMs, width, height, frameCount, quality}; cancel discards it. A recording stops itself after maxDurationMs or when its tab closes; the next stop or status returns its result with endedBecause.

tab.description: The tab to act on: the id navigate or tabs new returned (or a lent tab's id from tabs list), or a chosen id like `work-mail` given to tabs new.

path.description: start: output file ending in .mkv, .webm or .mp4; absolute inside the file roots (in a private folder you own), or relative (saved in a private folder in the first root).

quality.description: start: JPEG quality of captured frames (default 90).

maxDurationMs.description: start: stop automatically after this long (default 900000).

codex.instructions:
browse drives the user's real Chrome-family browser through the browse extension, so logins, extensions and open tabs are already there and the user can watch or take over. Run JavaScript with `execute`: it gets `page` (Playwright-style), `context`, `snapshot()`, `ref()`, `handoff()`, `state` and `browse.<tool>()` for every browse tool. `return` a value to get it back; one script can do many steps.

Tabs are the handle. Without `tab`, `page` has no tab until its first `page.goto(url)`, which opens a new background tab. Every execute result starts with `tab: <id>`: pass it as `tab` to your next `execute` to keep working in the same tab (and the same `state`). Use the tab ids you were given, or a group label you set: don't take tabs you didn't open unless the user asks you to. `context.newPage()` opens another tab; popups a page opens are yours to use. `tabs` lists every agent tab and the ones the user lent.

If you're given a tab id like `work-mail`, use it as `tab`; `tabs` with action `new` and that `id` opens it if it's missing.

Use one loop: inspect, act, verify.
- Inspect with `await snapshot()` before choosing anything. Prefer the returned refs: `await ref("e12").click()`. Fall back to accessible locators (`page.getByRole(...)`, `getByLabel(...)`), then CSS.
- Act with the narrowest stable control, and keep dependent steps in one `execute` while transient UI is open.
- Verify with a fresh page read (`page.url()`, a heading, or a new snapshot). A click that returned, or a handoff the user acknowledged, is not proof the task succeeded.

When only a person can proceed — login, 2FA, passkey, captcha or payment confirmation — call `handoff("what the user should do")` and wait. Pass `start` for an action that itself blocks. Never solve a captcha yourself and never retry-loop a blocked site; if a challenge is interactive or the site refuses the visit, hand off or stop and tell the user.

The code runs in a small sandboxed engine on the relay, not Node: no require/import, fs, process or fetch (use `page.evaluate` for things that belong to the page, `files` for files). Unsupported Playwright calls throw an error naming what to use instead.

When finished, close the tabs you opened (`await page.close()`, or the `tabs` tool with action `close`). `status` reports the relay and the connected browsers.

If a call fails because no browser is connected (the extension isn't added, paired or open), `status` says why in `nextStep`: pass that step to the user and wait for them instead of retrying.

tools.name: execute
tools.description: Run JavaScript that drives the browser: the user's real Chrome-family browser, through the browse extension. The code is an async function body (a single expression is returned; `return` a value to get it back) running in a small sandboxed JavaScript engine on the relay: no Node, no require/import, no fs, process or fetch (fetch belongs to the page: use page.evaluate). Synchronous code stops after about 2 seconds without an await. The result has the returned value (JSON, or the string as is), console output, warnings, and what happened to the page (URL changes, navigations, handoffs, a bot challenge: hand interactive ones to the user with handoff(), never solve or retry-loop them). Return a screenshot (`return await page.screenshot()`) to see it. Tabs are the handle: without `tab`, `page.goto(url)` opens a new tab; the result starts with `tab: <id>`, which you pass as `tab` to the next execute to continue there (with the same `state`). Close tabs you opened when you're done (`page.close()`).

code.description:
JavaScript (an async function body). Globals:
- page: a Playwright-style Page for the tab passed as `tab`; without one it has no tab until its first goto(url), which opens a new tab. goto(url, {waitUntil, timeout}), url(), title(), content(), evaluate(fn | string, arg), $eval/$$eval, waitForTimeout/Selector/URL/LoadState/Function, click/fill/type/press/hover/selectOption/check/uncheck(selector, ...), locator(selector), getByRole/Text/Label/Placeholder/TestId/AltText/Title, frameLocator, keyboard.press/type, mouse.click/move/wheel, screenshot({path, fullPage}), goBack/goForward/reload, setViewportSize, close(). Locators: click, dblclick, fill, clear, type, pressSequentially, press, hover, check, uncheck, selectOption, setInputFiles, textContent, innerText, innerHTML, inputValue, getAttribute, isVisible/Hidden/Checked/Enabled/Disabled, count, all, first, last, nth, filter, locator, getBy*, waitFor, evaluate, evaluateAll, allTextContents, boundingBox, screenshot, dragTo. Selectors are CSS or Playwright selectors (role=button[name="Save"], text=Sign in, >> nth=0, iframe >> frame >> ...). Locators are strict: one element.
- context.newPage() (a new tab), context.pages() (the tabs this execute works in and their popups); browser.contexts().
- snapshot(options?) → a compact outline with refs (options: find, diff, delta, interactive, within, mode: "aria"); ref("e12") → a locator for a snapshot ref. Prefer snapshot + ref over guessing selectors.
- handoff(message, {timeoutMs?, start?}) when only the user can proceed (login, 2FA, captcha, payment); demonstrate(message) to watch the user do a flow.
- screenshotWithLabels(), screenshotDiff({baseline}), network.start/status/stop/cancel, pageConsole.start/read/stop, webmcp.list/call(name, input).
- browse.<tool>(args): any browse tool directly (navigate, snapshot, click, fill, type, press, select, hover, drag, scroll, eval, wait_for, dialog, upload, emulate, webmcp, screenshot, screenshot_diff, network, console, recording, tabs, handoff, demonstrate, status, settings); they act in `page`'s tab unless you pass `tab` (browse.navigate without one opens a tab for `page`); returns its JSON and throws its error.
- files.path(name), files.write(name, data), files.read(name, encoding?) inside the file roots (files.dir, files.roots).
- state: an object kept with the tab between execute calls that pass it as `tab` (JSON values only).
- console.log/warn/error (shown in the result), setTimeout/clearTimeout/setInterval/clearInterval.

timeoutMs.description: Overall timeout in milliseconds (paused while handoff waits on the user); default 60000, 0 for none. Includes waiting behind another execute in the same tab.

tab.description: The tab `page` stands for: the `tab` an earlier execute (or navigate, tabs) returned, or a chosen id like `work-mail` given to tabs new. Leave it out to start without a tab; page.goto(url) then opens one.

tools.name: status
tools.description: Report the relay, the connected browsers (ids to pass as `browser` when opening a tab), pairing state and what to do when no browser is connected (`nextStep`), and the tabs you can use.

tools.name: tabs
tools.description: List, open or close tabs. Tabs are the handle every other tool takes as `tab`. `list` returns every agent tab and every tab the user lent (tab id, id when one was chosen, url, title, group, options, lent, lastUsed, busy and browser). An id or group from that list tells you which tabs you opened; use only those unless the user asks you to touch another. `new` opens a background tab (at `url`, else about:blank), waits for it to load and returns its `tab` id; `navigate` without `tab` does the same. Give it an `id` like `work-mail` to name the tab yourself: opening that id again returns the tab it already names, without navigating it, and the id survives browser restarts (use it as `tab` in every tool). `close` needs explicit tabs: `tab`, `tabs` or a whole `group`; a lent tab is given back to the user instead of closed. Tabs open in the background and never take focus from the user; close the ones you opened when you're done.

group.description: new: the new tab's group label. list: only that group's tabs. close: close every tab opened with that group (and their popups).

allowedOrigins.description: When opening a tab: hosts or origins it may load (example.com, *.example.com, https://app.example.com, http://localhost:3000). Navigations elsewhere are refused or sent back to about:blank; private and loopback addresses need an exact entry. Popups inherit it.

readOnly.description: When opening a tab: only read it (snapshots, screenshots, page state); input and later navigation are refused.

keepVisible.description: When opening a tab: keep it focused to the page between calls, for apps that pause while hidden. Pages can notice.

browser.description: When opening a tab: which connected browser, by the id or name `status` lists. Defaults to the first connected one.

action.description: What to do. Defaults to list.

id.description: new: an id you choose for the tab, like `work-mail` (lowercase letters, digits and dashes). Every tool takes it as `tab`. Opening with an id that already exists returns that tab without navigating it; the tab keeps the id when the browser restarts, and is never closed as idle.

url.description: new: the URL to open (else about:blank).

tab.description: close: the tab to close: its numeric id, or a chosen id like `work-mail`.

tabs.description: close: several tabs to close, by numeric or chosen id.

idleMinutes.description: close: only tabs no call used for this long. It narrows tab, tabs or group; it doesn't pick tabs on its own, and never a tab with a chosen id.
